critical_errors.location: thm:lck-vaisman-volume and the following symmetry paragraph
critical_errors.issue: The chapter defines Vaisman by parallel Lee form and permits lambda=0, so its prescribed-volume uniqueness theorem includes all Kahler metrics and is false. On X=C^n/(Z+iZ)^n, n>=2, omega_t=(i/2)(t dz_1 wedge dbar z_1+t^(-1) dz_2 wedge dbar z_2+sum_{j>=3}dz_j wedge dbar z_j), t>0, are distinct Kahler, hence Vaisman under the given definition, metrics with Lee class zero and identical pointwise volume. Invariance under the zero Lee and anti-Lee fields is automatic. The canonical rank-two real foliation and contraction-to-basic-volume discussion likewise require nonzero Lee form.
critical_errors.repair_hint: Require lambda not identically zero in the Vaisman prescribed-volume theorem and its canonical-foliation discussion, or include this requirement in the Vaisman definition. For a parallel Lee form on a compact manifold this is equivalent to strict LCK: an exact parallel form vanishes because its potential attains a maximum. If retaining a Kahler prescribed-volume case, fix a Kahler class as well.

reference_checks.location: chapter_lck.tex: The Lee form and the Kahler covering
reference_checks.details: Definitions3.16,3.21,3.25,3.27, Remarks3.17,3.20 and Claim3.28 (archived text2144-2265) match the LCK tensor equation, conformal Lee change, covering form e^(-F)pi^*omega, homothety character and automorphic/weight bundle interpretation. Claim3.28 footnote explicitly acknowledges the constant choice of flat trivialization, consistent with the chapter's later gauge identification.

Conjecture4.14 asks strict positivity of Lee degree against every Gauduchon metric, and Remark4.16 identifies this with pseudoeffectivity of the ordinary Bott-Chern Lee-curvature class. The abstract specifies curvature -d(I theta); Remark4.15 gives d theta^c=-d^c theta. Since I theta=4pi lambda^c under the chapter convention, -d(I theta)=4pi kappa_lambda, so the sign and positivity cone match. The chapter retains the conjectural status and restricts to strict LCK.

Definition18.34 is ker d_theta on forms with values in a flat bundle modulo image partial_theta barpartial_theta; Definition18.36 places the LCK class there. Its real (1,1) part in the fixed trivialization is exactly the chapter's quotient by D_lambda of real smooth functions. A nonzero constant normalization does not change the image. The conformal gauge identification multiplication by e^(-a) is correct.

The exact source item(3), printed pp683-684, archived text34188-34201, asks whether Gauduchon LCK metrics with the same Lee class, twisted Bott-Chern class and volume form coincide. The chapter makes the flat bundle identification explicit and properly retains the assertion as an open question; older Vaisman-only uniqueness results returned by theorem search were not substituted.

reference_checks.source: OV24-Vaisman-CY arXiv2206.08808v2 Theorem4.1, Remark2.5, Remark2.6, Proposition3.1
reference_checks.details: Theorem4.1, archived text310-314, exactly retains invariant positive volume, equal total volume, same Lee CLASS and uniqueness. Proposition3.1, archived244-245, fixes the Lee field up to a real multiplier, and Remark2.5 gives holomorphic commuting Killing Lee/anti-Lee fields. But Remark2.5 uses a complex one-dimensional canonical foliation and Remark2.6 normalizes Lee length to1. OV24-LCK Remark3.18, archived2163-2166, explicitly notes the usual tacit nonexact Lee assumption. The excerpt's broader explicit definition introduces the zero-Lee counterexample recorded above. The known strict Vaisman theorem is not disputed.
